# 1 Clement Chapter 55 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 55 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_055_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 55

**55:1** But to bring forward examples from among the Gentiles as well: many kings and rulers, in times of plague, when moved by oracles, have given themselves over to death, so that by their own blood they might rescue their fellow-citizens. Many have left their own cities, that the rebellions among them might come to an end.

**55:2** We know many among ourselves who gave themselves up to bondage so that they might ransom others. Many sold themselves into slavery, and with the price paid for themselves they fed others.

**55:3** Many women, being strengthened through the grace of God, performed many deeds of manly courage.

**55:4** The blessed Judith, when the city was under siege, asked the elders to allow her to go forth into the camp of the strangers.

**55:5** Therefore she gave herself up to danger and went out for love of her country and of her besieged people — and the LORD delivered Holofernes into the hand of a woman.

**55:6** No less so did the blessed Esther, who, being perfect in faith, exposed herself to danger in order to rescue the twelve tribes of Israel from imminent destruction. For by fasting and self-abasement she entreated the all-seeing Master; and he, beholding the humility of her soul, delivered the people for whose sake she had exposed herself to peril.

---

*LOGOS renders according to the standard Greek text of Codex Alexandrinus with attention to formal correspondence.*
